meta.title: Orchard — a garden weather station
meta.subtitle: Round 1 of 3
meta.headline: First, what is this thing actually for?
meta.lede: You have described a weather station twice and a frost alarm once. Those are different projects. Five questions settle which one we are building and what you want handed back — then the next round gets specific.
steps: Change or reject what does not fit
meta.closingAsk: Update the scope from these answers, then tell me what is still open.

scope.label: What we're trying to achieve
scope.text: Not agreed yet. This round asks whether the station is a frost alarm or a weather record.

scope.label: What we hand over
scope.text: Not agreed yet. This round asks whether you want a plan, a working thing, or a quick trial.

scope.label: What's in and what's out
scope.text: Assumed for now: one station in one orchard, no second site and no sharing with anyone else.
scope.assumption: Nothing you have said suggests a second site, so I am assuming one station until the goal is agreed.

scope.label: How we know it's done
scope.text: Assumed for now: it is done when it survives one cold night and tells you something you acted on.
scope.assumption: A real cold night is the only honest test, so I am assuming that until you tell me otherwise.

scope.label: Fixed facts we work inside
scope.text: Mains power in the shed, twelve metres from the mast. No cloud account — the data stays at home.
scope.assumption: Taken from your first message; I am treating both as fixed until you say they are negotiable.

constraints.label: Power:
constraints.text: mains socket in the shed, 12 m from the mast

constraints: No cloud account — the data stays on the home network

context.title: Site context
context.note: The orchard runs down a `north-facing` slope. Cold air pools at the bottom, which is the whole reason you raised this.

cards.title: Mast
cards.body: A 3 m pole at the high corner, clear of the hedge.

cards.title: Shed
cards.body: Houses the mains supply and whatever does the recording.

items.desc: cold air pooling at the low end of a slope
the temperature at which the air gives up its moisture

blocks.heading: Note
blocks.text: Nothing here has to survive a power cut for more than an hour.

questions.context: You mentioned frost twice and wind once. Which one the station is really for decides what goes up the mast first, and how soon it is useful.
breakdown: Frost only: fewer sensors, and one number to get right.
Everything: a fuller picture, but nothing is finished for weeks.
questions.question: What is the station mainly for?
questions.why: Frost is the one that costs you fruit, and it needs the fewest sensors to answer honestly.
questions.switchIf: Choose the general record if you want the data more than you want to be woken up.

options.label: Frost warning
options.detail: One job done properly: tell you the night before.

options.label: A general weather record
options.detail: Everything logged, nothing acted on automatically.

options.label: Both from the start
options.detail: Twice the mounting and twice the debugging up front.

questions.context: A warning is only worth building if it reaches someone who can act on it while there is still time to act.
breakdown: Just you: simplest, and you already check your phone.
You and whoever is on the land: more useful, more to set up.
questions.question: Who needs to act on a frost warning?
questions.why: Sending to one person is a setting; sending to several is an account system, which is a different project.
questions.switchIf: Choose the shared version if someone else is usually the one out there at dawn.

options.label: Just you
options.detail: One phone, one number, nothing to administer.

options.label: You and one other person
options.detail: Two destinations, still no accounts needed.

options.label: Anyone who subscribes
options.detail: Needs sign-ups, and someone to run them.

questions.context: Lighting candles or covering blossom takes time. How far ahead the warning has to arrive changes what the station has to be able to do.
breakdown: It is cold now: simple to build, and often too late to help.
It will be cold by dawn: needs a forecast rule, not just a reading.
questions.example: A dew point reading at 9 p.m. plus a clear sky tells you roughly where the temperature will land by 4 a.m.
questions.question: How much warning do you need?
questions.why: A few hours is the difference between knowing and doing, and the maths for it is well established.
questions.switchIf: Choose the live reading if you are up at that hour anyway and would rather trust your own eyes.

options.label: Tell me when it is freezing
options.detail: A plain threshold on the current reading.

options.label: Warn me a few hours ahead
options.detail: A dew point rule, checked each evening.

options.label: A full overnight forecast
options.detail: Needs outside data and a lot more tuning.

questions.context: You have not said whether you want something to read or something to run, and the two take very different amounts of your time.
breakdown: A plan: you build it, at your own pace, with the decisions made.
A working version: faster to something real, less room to change your mind.
questions.question: What should I hand you at the end of this?
questions.why: You have the shed, the mast and the weekends, so a plan you can follow is worth more than code you did not write.
questions.switchIf: Choose the working version if you would rather have something running this month than understood.

options.label: A build plan
options.detail: Ordered steps, parts list, and what to do first.

options.label: A working first version
options.detail: Something that records a reading by the weekend.

options.label: A quick trial first
options.detail: One sensor on the windowsill to see if it holds up.

questions.context: Whatever I hand back can include some extras. Picking them now stops me guessing and stops the plan sprawling.
breakdown: Parts list: useful if you are buying, noise if you already have the kit.
Wiring notes: worth it only if you are doing the wiring yourself.
questions.question: Which of these would you actually use?
questions.why: You said you have most of the parts already, so the wiring notes earn their place and the shopping list mostly does not.
questions.switchIf: Add the parts list too if you would rather order everything in one go and be done with it.

options.label: Wiring notes
options.detail: What connects to what, and which end is which.

options.label: A test for cold night one
options.detail: How to tell whether it actually worked.

options.label: A parts list
options.detail: Everything to buy, with rough prices.

options.label: A running cost estimate
options.detail: What it costs to leave switched on all year.
